title: Why SaaS growth stalls: cancellation beats paid marketing, and how to raise the ceiling
summary: Jason Cohen explains why every SaaS hits a growth ceiling: paid acquisition flattens (the "elephant curve") while cancellations scale with customer count. He shows how to compute the ceiling, diagnose churn, raise prices to move into a better market, and build strategy around an ideal customer who loves your weaknesses.

principles.text: Compute your growth ceiling: new MRR per month divided by monthly cancellation rate. That is the max you reach if nothing changes.
principles.quote: It's just the new dollars per month divided by the monthly cancellation rate. That is the max you will grow if you don't change something.

principles.text: Paid channels don't scale with your size but churn does, so cancellation eventually beats paid marketing.
principles.quote: Marketing doesn't care. Like AdWords doesn't care how many customers you have. It still just works the same way. It doesn't scale with you, but cancellation does.

principles.text: 'Too expensive' is rarely the real cancellation reason. Find the root cause (missing feature, wrong expectation) and fix that, not the price.
principles.quote: The thing they wanted is the thing to fix. Not lowering the price.

principles.text: Catch at-risk customers before they leave by finding behaviors that differ between cancellers and stayers, then reach out early.
principles.quote: how what characteristics are different on the people that cancel than the people that stay? These are your early signals.

principles.text: When unsure where to cut churn, start with onboarding: most cancellations happen early, so improving the start has the biggest financial effect.
principles.quote: Almost always onboarding has the most impact with cancellation.

principles.text: Your price is probably too low. Raising it can move you from hobbyists to serious business customers who stick, and sign-ups may even rise.
principles.quote: there's no way your prices are optimal. Full stop.
